name: Amos
description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: The words of Amos, who was among the herdmen of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.

note.label: Amos 1: For Three Transgressions and For Four

points: Notice what's being said here by Amos, but notice the actions of Amaziah. Amaziah was more concerned with protecting the king's institution instead of hearing the word of the Lord. And it's the same thing that's going on today. Why? Because the things written afore time was written for our learning. Instead of correcting the leaders or some of the teachers in these congregations with their ridiculous doctrines or ridiculous accusations, they prefer we not speak at all. It's the same thing here that we reading with Amaziah and Amos.

note.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

points: Amaziah the priest of Bethel: he's complaining about Amos prophesying. The land is not able to bear all his words: the land can't take the prophecies of Amos. Amos was telling the northern kingdom, y'all going into slavery soon.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: Amos hath conspired against thee in the midst of the house of Israel: now this is old. Just like what Jeremiah went through, Amos is going through. Amaziah was a priest, was northern kingdom, trying to put a lie on Amos to get him put to death, saying Amos is come against the king. That's what's happening. Our own people is going to do this to us.
Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent word to Jeroboam that Amos had conspired against him and that the land could not bear his words.

note.label: Amos 7: The Plumb Line and the Prophet's Job

points: For thus Amos saith, Jeroboam shall die by the sword: you see how direct he was? That's somebody who's direct and fearless. Who's Jeroboam? That's the king. Let's put some perspective. Imagine you going to Donald Trump and telling him you going to die. What you think them secret service going to do to you? Oh man. You putting yourself in harm's way.

O thou seer, go, flee thee away into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there: Amaziah came and said, yo, Amos, go to Judah. Stop coming here in northern kingdom land and telling us about God. We don't want to hear that. Go to Judah. We got our own prophets here.
Amaziah told Amos to flee into the land of Judah, eat bread there, and prophesy no more at Bethel, for it was the king's chapel and court.

note.label: Amos 7: The Plumb Line and the Prophet's Job

points: Amos answered that he was no prophet nor a prophet's son, but a herdman and a gatherer of sycamore fruit whom the Lord took as he followed the flock and sent to prophesy unto his people Israel.

note.label: Amos 7: The Plumb Line and the Prophet's Job

points: The Most High showed Amos a basket of summer fruit and said the end is come upon his people of Israel, and he will not again pass by them anymore.

note.label: Amos 8: A Basket of Summer Fruit and a Famine of the Word
